q: For any trapped sample of gas, we can measure its temperature, the volume of the space it occupies, its pressure against the confining wall and its ____.
e: For any trapped sample of gas, we can measure its temperature, the volume of the space it occupies, its pressure against the confining wall and its mass. Pressure, volume and temperature of a fixed amount of gas are tied together by the gas laws.

q: The units of temperature are degree Celsius, degree Fahrenheit and ____.
e: The units of temperature are degree Celsius, degree Fahrenheit and Kelvin. Gas laws use Kelvin because that scale starts at absolute zero, where particle motion would stop.

q: The boiling point of water is ____ $^{\circ} C$.
e: The boiling point of water is 100 ^ degrees C. The boiling point of water is ^ degrees C.

q: normal human body temperature is ____ $^{\circ} C$.
e: Normal human body temperature is 37 ^ degrees C. Normal human body temperature is ^ degrees C.
Absolute zero is 0 K. Absolute zero is 0 K, the point where gas volume in Charles's law would theoretically hit zero. That temperature is also -273 degrees C on the Celsius scale.
1000 cm^3 = 1000 mL = 1 L = 1 dm^3. One litre is the same volume as one cubic decimetre, which is also 1000 mL or 1000 cm3.

q: A gas exerts a ____ on the walls of any container.
e: A gas exerts a force on the walls of any container. A gas has no shape or volume of its own, so it takes the shape and volume of its container.

q: Pressure is in fact the force that acts on a given ____.
e: Pressure is in fact the force that acts on a given area. Gas pressure is the force of collisions on a unit area of the wall.

q: 1 $Nm^{-2}$ = 1 Pa (____ is SI unit of pressure).
e: 1 Nm^-2 = 1 Pa (pascal is SI unit of pressure). The SI unit of pressure is the pascal, one newton per square metre.

q: The effects of pressure are observed in the mixture of gases surrounding the Earth-our ____.
e: The effects of pressure are observed in the mixture of gases surrounding the Earth-our atmosphere. The mixture of gases around Earth is the atmosphere, and that mixture exerts pressure.

q: The atmosphere is composed of nitrogen, oxygen, ____ and other minor constituents.
e: The atmosphere is composed of nitrogen, oxygen, argon and other minor constituents. About 78 percent of clean dry air is nitrogen.

q: The actual value of atmospheric pressure depends on location, temperature and ____ conditions.
e: The actual value of atmospheric pressure depends on location, temperature and weather conditions. Atmospheric pressure changes with location, temperature and weather.

q: Instruments used for measuring atmospheric pressure and gas pressure are barometer and ____, respectively.
e: Instruments used for measuring atmospheric pressure and gas pressure are barometer and manometer, respectively. A barometer measures atmospheric pressure, and a manometer measures the pressure of a confined gas. A manometer measures gas pressure by comparing it with atmospheric pressure.

q: Standard atmospheric pressure (1 atm) is equal to the pressure that supports a column of ____ exactly 760 mm high at 0 $^{\circ} C$ at sea level.
e: Standard atmospheric pressure (1 atm) is equal to the pressure that supports a column of mercury exactly 760 mm high at 0 ^ degrees C at sea level. One atmosphere is 101325 pascals, newtons per square metre.

q: The mmHg unit is also the same as the ____.
e: The mmHg unit is also the same as the torr. The torr is defined to be equal to one millimetre of mercury.
1 atm = 101,325 Pa. One atmosphere is 101325 pascals, newtons per square metre. A pascal is one newton of force on each square metre.

q: The mass of a gas can be determined by weighing the gas in an enclosed container by gram or ____.
e: The mass of a gas can be determined by weighing the gas in an enclosed container by gram or kilogram. A gas has no shape or volume of its own, so it takes the shape and volume of its container. The SI base unit of mass is the kilogram, symbol kg.
